Would you have any tips for that? I've been learning at some JapanesePod and using Anki on my phone. What else could I do and how did you become proficient in Japanese?

Hmm, sure, I can share what's seemed to work for me. Apps can be good for drilling/testing, but I found carrying a small notepad and writing everyday helped a lot.

Learn to write in Japanese as soon as possible, and avoid studying or reading anything in romaji.

I found flashcards for the first 4 grade levels of kanji, which helped me learn them. Keep a stack in your pocket so you can flip through them anytime you are killing time.

Once I had some basic skills, I focused mostly on input, reading/listening, and the output part, speaking/writing, got better along with it. For that, textbooks are OK, but I also enjoyed reading lots of children's books. I found the language to be more natural and useful than manga, and the stories are fun. Also, listening to anime in Japanese works but I had to watch the same episodes multiple times before new vocabulary would sink in.

Of course, emailing or chatting with native speakers if you can is great too :)
